# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 83 (Bu-Vb Pc83)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc83
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 83
**Title (English, from literature):** Entering a royal compound unannounced
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 83 (titled *Antepura* in the Pali tradition) regulates the conduct of Buddhist monks with respect to entering royal residences. The rule stipulates that a monk who enters the bedchamber or private quarters of an anointed king unannounced must confess the offense (*pācittiya*) [Stache-Rosen 1984]. In the rule's origin story (*nidāna*), Ānanda walks thoughtlessly into the private quarters of Queen Mallikā and sees her unclothed; modern scholars note that the prohibition primarily aimed to safeguard monks from suspicion of sexual impropriety, inappropriate political influence, or espionage within royal palaces [Blackstone 1995; Hüsken 1997]. The narrative framework of the text also incorporates an exposition on the ten dangers of entering a royal palace [Bapat and Hirakawa 1970].

  DharmaNexus strongly corroborates this, showing near-verbatim text reuse between Pācittiya 83 (§1.2.18–1.3.53) and the *Dasakanipāta* of the Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 10.45, 98% similarity over 10,000 characters), alongside reuse in the *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* and various Khandhaka sections [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language matches generated by DharmaNexus further align the rule with Sanskrit Prātimokṣa passages and Tibetan Vinaya commentaries, including the *Vinayasūtraṭīkā* [DharmaNexus].
